content:
Sara K: Noticing a reproducible SSE sequencing glitch when sessions get load-migrated across sequencer nodes. Steps: open multiplexed SSE client, send events rapidly, force migration via route drain, client sometimes receives reorder or duplicate 'delta' events.
Omar: any recent changes to sequencer lease expiry? We pushed a change to extend soft-lease by 250ms last week to reduce drop rate.
Sara K: yep that was the change. Traces show both nodes briefly think they can emit sequence numbers for same session id. Example log snippet:
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] seq-node-a: lease_acquire session=sz-22 lease=holder ttl=100ms
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] seq-node-a: emit seq=101 session=sz-22
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] router: migrate session=sz-22 -> seq-node-b
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] seq-node-b: lease_acquire session=sz-22 lease=holder ttl=100ms
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] seq-node-b: emit seq=102 session=sz-22
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] client_recv seq=102 session=sz-22
[2026-03-25T09:12:01Z] client_recv seq=101 session=sz-22
Felix: Sequence numbers are supposed to be globally monotonic per session. Did we accidentally allow overlapping holder windows?
Omar: the soft-lease is intended to avoid stalls during GC, but we left a grace where old holder can still emit for 250ms after a migration signal. That seems to be the culprit.
Vera (console): Console shows brief spikes in "inflight_events" and some customers filed tickets about "messages out of order". We should flag routes where sequencer.lease_grace > 0 for customer visibility.
Sara K: quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce soft-lease grace to 15ms for multiplexed sessions, 2) emit a telemetry facet sequencer.overlap_detect when two nodes emit adjacent seq numbers within 1s, 3) add console indicator "sequencer migration" with a hover that explains possible transient reorder.
Felix: alternative is to strictly hand off with a flush/ack handshake: old node must ack its last emit before new node starts. That's zero-reorder but increases handoff latency. Tradeoff doc needed.
Omar: agree on telemetry + short-term grace reduction on canary. We should only apply aggressive reduction for high-throughput MPX sessions.
ops-bot: note: potential billing risk — duplicated emits can be double-counted. Please coordinate with billing if we change replay/dedupe semantics.
Vera (console): I'll add a temporary tooltip and an orange badge for routes with >0.1% sequencer.overlap_detect in the last 10m. Low-risk UI change.
Sara K: I'll push a canary patch to runtime/sequencer/2026-03-25/reduce-grace -> eu-canary with debug telemetry.
DeployBot: deploy started for runtime/sequencer/2026-03-25/reduce-grace -> eu-canary (id: d-9962).
DeployBot: canary finished: 6 instances updated, health OK.
Omar: early canary metrics: sequencer.overlap_detect dropped from 0.65% -> 0.04% on mpx routes. Client-side reorder reports down from 12/day -> 1/day in sampled customers.
Felix: ok promising. Next steps: 1) tradeoff doc on flush-handshake vs grace tuning (Felix/Omar), 2) billing dedupe proposal (Ops/Billing), 3) console annotation shipped (Vera).
Vera (console): queued the UI patch, will ship to prod after brief review. Also adding a small analytics card to surface overlap metric on route pages.
Sara K: repro harness and logs uploaded to the doc repo. We'll monitor for 6h then consider broader rollout. Thanks team.
Omar: pinging @billing-eng in separate thread about dedupe window suggestion (10s idempotency by session+seq).
Felix: note for follow-up: check interactions with SSE resume/last-event-id semantics; might be different than WS.
Sara K: closing the loop once we get billing confirmation and 6h of canary metrics.
